company_name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited

inputs.share_count_basis: Paid-up equity share capital Rs 460.79 crore at Rs 2 face value as at 30 Sep 2026 (Q2 FY2027 results, line 656) = 2,303.95m shares, after the ~143.8m shares issued for NQXT in Dec 2025. Basic EPS = diluted EPS in the Q2 FY2027 statement, so there are no dilutive securities. The Metrics CSV FY2026 figure of 2,199.2m is the weighted average for FY2026, not the period-end count. Held FLAT: there is no SBC to charge, and the only issuance channel is non-SBC related-party share swaps of the NQXT type, which is modelled as a bear-case risk in the narrative rather than a mechanical dilution path.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 Sep 2026 consolidated balance sheet (Q2 FY2027 results). Borrowings non-current 43,466.21 + current 14,250.30 = Rs 57,716.51 crore; lease liabilities 7,757.92 + 523.79 = Rs 8,281.71 crore (lease treatment A: leases are debt). Less cash and cash equivalents 5,074.45, bank balances other than cash 2,955.72, and current investments (mutual funds etc.) 1,361.99 = Rs 9,392.16 crore cash-like, matching the company's own net-debt definition. Net debt Rs 56,606.06 crore = INR 566,060.6m. The company's reported FY2026 Net Debt of Rs 44,164 crore excludes leases and nets additional financial assets.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero filer. FY2026 annual report consolidated statement of profit and loss and employee benefits expense (note 24) carry no share-based payment line; the only ESOP reference in the report is to the SEBI regulation name. Recorded as 0 and kept visible at 0% in the driver paths.
inputs.interest_income_source: FY2026 annual report consolidated cash flow statement / segment note: Interest Income Rs 1,394.50 crore (line 25767; Q2 FY2027 segment note line 839). Stripped from owner FCF because cash, bank balances and current investments are credited in the net-debt bridge. The forward component build starts from EBITDA (company definition excludes other income), so forward flows exclude it by construction.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases FY2021-FY2026 (last buyback FY2020, Rs 1,960 crore). Flat count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for; immaterial here because SBC is zero.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% (Nov 2026). Equity risk premium for India 6.0%. Beta 1.0 (large-cap listed infrastructure with concession-backed cash flows). Plus a 0.5pp corporate-governance / related-party premium for Adani Group overhang (Hindenburg-era SEBI matters largely closed, SC declined SIT/CBI transfer Jan 2024, DOJ moved to dismiss the Adani Green indictment; the residual is minority-shareholder exposure to intra-group deal structures such as the NQXT share swap, not a binary disqualifier). Cost of equity = 6.5 + 1.0 x 6.0 + 0.5 = 13.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~7.5% INR-equivalent (S&P BBB, Moody's Baa3 stable; USD bonds plus hedging cost), after-tax at 25% = 5.6%. Weights at market: equity ~Rs 4.46 lakh crore vs net debt incl. leases Rs 0.57 lakh crore = 88/12. WACC = 0.88 x 13.0 + 0.12 x 5.6 = 12.1%, rounded to 12.0%. Risk is charged ONCE: the governance premium lives in the WACC, the same WACC applies to all three scenarios, and the probability weights carry only operational and leverage axes.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. Lease liabilities of Rs 8,281.71 crore (30 Sep 2026) are included in net debt; lease principal (Rs 632 crore FY2026) is NOT deducted from the flows; lease interest is in the WACC not the flows. D&A path includes right-of-use depreciation, so cash-tax EBIT is after the full D&A line. Lease-asset renewal is captured by carrying the lease liability as perpetual debt rather than through a capex line; the capex path is purchase of PPE / CWIP only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once. Flows are consolidated (EBITDA includes subsidiaries at 100%); non-controlling interests of Rs 3,081.71 crore (30 Sep 2026 book) are deducted once in the equity bridge. FY2026 NCI share of profit was -Rs 24 crore and H1 FY2027 Rs 90 crore, so book is a fair proxy. Matching-asset rule: JV/associate investments (Rs 3,157.61 crore) and non-current investments (Rs 879.56 crore) are added at book because their income (share of JV profit, FVTOCI dividends) is excluded from EBITDA. Non-current bank deposits (Rs 3,109.91 crore) and loans to JVs/others (Rs 1,366.41 crore) are added at book as the matching assets of the stripped interest income. Remaining 'other financial assets' (Rs 3,243 crore non-current, Rs 1,535 crore current: security deposits, receivables, derivatives) are NOT added; whatever interest they earn is a small conservative omission.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US, capex-heavy infrastructure; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 with owner-fcf-adaptations for INR WACC, leases, NCI and SBC-zero). Fresh build, no prior DCF or memory entry. FY0 is FY2026 (year to 31 Mar 2026); Y1 is FY2027, for which management guides revenue Rs 44,000-46,000 crore, EBITDA Rs 26,000-27,000 crore and capex Rs 15,000-17,000 crore (raised twice during the year). H1 FY2027 actuals: revenue +21%, EBITDA margin ~59.6%. Longer-term anchor: 'Ambition 2031' to double revenue and EBITDA to >Rs 90,000 crore and >Rs 50,000 crore by FY2031 with a Rs 90,000-100,000 crore five-year capex envelope and a net debt/EBITDA ceiling of 2.5x (1.9x FY2026). The base case haircuts that ambition by roughly 20% on revenue. Cash tax ramps from ~12% of EBIT toward the 25% statutory rate as Section 80-IA port/SEZ tax holidays expire and MAT credits are consumed (FY2026 cash taxes paid Rs 1,514 crore on segment EBIT of Rs 17,592 crore = 8.6%; P&L effective rate 13.9%). Owner FCF FY2026 (INR 36,414m) is depressed by a capex-supercycle year (capex 39.5% of revenue); the component build is used instead of carrying that margin forward. Horizon 10 years because capex intensity is still normalising past year 5. Terminal cap multiple 18x owner FCF (below the 20x default: terminal-heavy, trade-cycle exposed). House and street bases coincide because SBC is zero; band_position is null by construction. Unlevered flows: finance costs (Rs 4,645 crore FY2026) are not in the flows; they are in the WACC and the net-debt deduction.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance-anchored base path (FY2027 guidance midpoint +16%, decaying to 10% by Y5; 5-year average ~12.8%). Historical revenue CAGRs of 23-25% include Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Haifa, Ocean Sparkle and NQXT acquisitions and are not a sustainable organic base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 25.7% exceeds EPS 5-yr CAGR 18.8% by >30%. Book equity is inflated by share issuance (FY2022 placements; FY2026 NQXT share swap, Rs ~23,000 crore of new equity), so equity CAGR overstates organic compounding. EPS and revenue are the better guide.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - 0 SBC - interest income (FY2021 56,023-17,582 = 38,441; FY2023 28,085-12,463 = 15,622; FY2026 50,359-13,945 = 36,414; INR m). The 5-yr owner-FCF CAGR of -1% against revenue +25% is capex timing (capex rose from 15.6% of revenue in FY2021 to 39.5% in FY2026), not deteriorating economics; EBITDA grew ~20%/yr over the same window. FCF CAGRs are therefore not used to set growth.

base.growth_note: Y1 17% sits between the FY2027 guidance midpoint (+16.2%) and the H1 run-rate (+21%); management has raised twice and historically beats. Decays to 5% by Y10. Implied FY2031 revenue ~Rs 70,600 crore vs the Rs 90,000 crore ambition (22% haircut).
base.margin_note: FY2026 59.0%, FY2027 guidance midpoint 58.9%. Drifts to 56.5% as lower-margin logistics, marine services and international terminals grow faster than domestic ports (73% margin); management's own ambition implies ~56% by FY2031.
base.capex_note: FY2027 guidance midpoint Rs 16,000 crore = 35.5% of Y1 revenue. Normalises toward 18% (D&A 13.5% plus growth capex) as the Ambition 2031 build-out completes.
base.tax_note: Ramps 12% -> 25% as 80-IA holidays expire; FY2026 cash rate 8.6% of EBIT, P&L rate 13.9%.
base.wc_note: Receivables-driven business: growth consumes ~4% of incremental revenue.

bull.growth_note: Top of guidance and the H1 run-rate held longer; FY2031 revenue ~Rs 78,500 crore, still below the Rs 90,000 crore ambition.

bear.growth_note: Bottom of FY2027 guidance then a trade slowdown; coal (~1/3 of volume) declines faster than container/liquid offsets; capex stays elevated relative to the revenue it delivers.

scenario_narratives.base: India's largest private port network keeps compounding a little below management's Ambition 2031: revenue +17% in FY2027 (guidance Rs 44,000-46,000 crore, raised twice) decaying to 5% by FY2036, which lands FY2031 revenue near Rs 70,600 crore against the Rs 90,000 crore ambition. EBITDA margin drifts from 59% to 56.5% as logistics, marine services and the NQXT/Haifa/Colombo international terminals (lower margin than the 73% domestic ports) grow faster than the core. Capex runs at the Rs 15,000-17,000 crore guidance in FY2027 (35.5% of revenue) and normalises toward 18% as the five-year Rs 90,000-100,000 crore programme completes, so owner FCF margin widens from ~17% to ~25% while net debt/EBITDA stays inside the 2.5x ceiling. Cash tax ramps from ~12% to 25% as 80-IA holidays expire. The bull/bear axes are: cargo volume growth versus the 1-billion-tonne 2030/31 target, the coal share of the mix (~1/3) versus container and liquid growth, whether capex intensity actually falls or keeps being raised, and whether group-level governance events reappear in the cost of capital.
scenario_narratives.bull: Trade tailwinds (China+1 manufacturing shift, containerisation, Red Sea rerouting favouring Mundra) hold cargo growth near 15% for several years and revenue grows 19%/17%/15% before decaying; FY2031 revenue reaches ~Rs 78,500 crore. Mix dilution is offset by operating leverage at Mundra and faster-than-expected NQXT/Haifa integration, so EBITDA margin holds near 59%. Capex falls to 17% of revenue by Y10 as the programme matures, tax holidays persist longer (cash rate reaches 24% only in Y10), and terminal growth is 5% nominal INR. Rating upgrades (S&P BBB, Moody's/Fitch stable) continue to compress funding costs, but the WACC is held at 12% so the bull is a flows story, not a discount-rate story.
scenario_narratives.bear: Revenue grows 13% in FY2027 (bottom of guidance) then slows to 4-7% as a global trade slowdown hits container volumes while import coal, still about a third of the mix, declines structurally as India shifts to coastal and domestic coal. Logistics and international terminals dilute EBITDA margin to 53%. Capex is raised again rather than cut (as in FY2027), staying at 36% of revenue in Y1 and 19% in Y10, and tax holidays expire fastest (25% cash rate from Y7). Related-party deal structures of the NQXT type recur, with minority shareholders diluted at terms set inside the group; and a group-level governance or regulatory event reopens the funding discount. Terminal growth 4%. This path is also where the 2.5x net debt/EBITDA ceiling binds and the Ambition 2031 build-out gets stretched.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the thesis rests on a debt-funded capex programme whose guidance was raised twice within FY2027, coal is about a third of volume and in structural decline, and the NQXT precedent shows related-party share issuance is a live channel for minority dilution. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it requires trade growth, margin hold through mix dilution and capex discipline to happen together. Governance risk is priced in the WACC (+50bp) and is deliberately NOT double-counted in these weights.

valuation_philosophy.summary: APSEZ is valued as an operating infrastructure compounder on unlevered owner FCF: EBITDA (company definition, ex-forex and other income) less D&A, cash tax, capex and working capital, discounted at a currency-matched 12% INR WACC that includes an explicit 50bp governance premium, with a 10-year horizon so the terminal year capitalises a normalised capex intensity rather than the current supercycle. Leases are treated as debt, NCI is deducted once in the bridge, JV/associate investments are added at book, and SBC is zero so house and street coincide. The valuation is terminal-heavy by nature of the asset; the sensitivity grid and required-return table are the honest read of how much depends on the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value dominates: a 1pp move in WACC or terminal growth moves value materially; see the sensitivity grid
Capex intensity may not normalise: FY2027 capex guidance was raised twice; if capex stays above 30% of revenue through Y5 owner FCF is well below the base path
Coal cargo (~1/3 of volume) structural decline outpacing container and liquid growth
Related-party transactions and share-swap acquisitions (NQXT precedent) diluting minorities outside the SBC line, which the flat share count does not capture
Group-level governance or regulatory events (Hindenburg-era SEBI matters, US DOJ/SEC Adani Green case) reopening the funding discount; priced at +50bp in WACC, not as a scenario
Cash tax rate rising faster than modelled as 80-IA holidays expire and MAT credits are used
FX: USD bonds and AUD/ILS/LKR assets create translation swings in reported earnings and net debt
Concession and tariff regulation (TAMP, state governments) at specific terminals
valuation_philosophy.price_implied_return_memo: What the market price implies: on the base-case flows the required-return table gives INR ~1,106/share at a 9% INR discount rate and ~1,004 at 10% (where the 18x terminal cap binds), both well below the current price; the sensitivity grid tops out around 1,004 even at WACC 10% / g 5.5%, and the bull case at 12% is ~967. The price therefore requires BOTH management's full Ambition 2031 trajectory (revenue and EBITDA doubling by FY2031 and continued double-digit growth beyond) AND an INR discount rate of roughly 9% or less, which is near the Indian risk-free rate plus a thin premium. Street targets reach the price mainly via 16-18x forward EV/EBITDA, i.e. an exit multiple the house model does not grant. This is a finding about the price, not a reason to re-derive the drivers: the operating assumptions are already anchored above guidance in year 1 and the per-share build deliberately does not credit acquisition-led growth that has historically been part-funded by share issuance.
